body:
Acting on your BUG-1436 finding rather than leaving it in the findings queue — I pulled it from batch:night-0920, and I think it wants `aida defer` rather than another retry. Your call on the defer; the batch removal I have already done because it was actively burning cycles.

WHAT IT WAS DOING. BUG-1436 ran its implementer phase 18:56:25 → 19:01:37, five minutes twelve, and produced nothing: `bug-1436-work` is exactly origin/main (c2b3c2f0c8), no code commit anywhere references the spec, the worktree is clean. It then shelved `no-pr`, retried, and attempt 2 has been live for a minute as I write this. It will do the same thing.

YOUR FINDING EXPLAINS IT COMPLETELY. 1,000 direct test-binary runs at process parallelism 16 on this kernel produced 0 failures, and local artifact searches did not recover the original panic. Acceptance requires the next real occurrence. So the implementer is not failing — it is correctly concluding there is nothing it can do, and the drain is reading that as a transient no-PR and retrying it.

THIS IS A SHAPE, NOT JUST A SPEC. `no-pr` is in the transient-retry set, which is right for a session that crashed or forgot `/aida-pr`. It is wrong for a session that ran to completion and correctly determined the work cannot be done yet. Those two produce an identical signal — a clean exit with no PR — and the recovery hint tells the reader to "resume the session and run `/aida-pr`", which on an empty branch would open a PR with no diff.

The five-minute phase duration is the tell that separates them from the other no-op shape I filed as BUG-1476: there the implementer exits in fifteen seconds because a PR already exists; here it spends five real minutes and concludes correctly. Same outcome, opposite causes, and both currently land as retryable.

WHY DEFER RATHER THAN REJECT OR PARK. The spec is not wrong and the work is not abandoned — it is waiting on an external event that will arrive on its own. That is exactly what `aida defer --until` is for, and unlike NeedsAttention it records the revisit trigger rather than filing the spec away. Suggested:

    aida defer BUG-1436 --until "a real Linux tick-lock failure is captured in CI or in local artifacts"

That takes it out of the open lens, keeps the trigger visible in `aida list --deferred`, and stops it re-entering a batch on the next refresh. I have not run it — status disposition is yours and this one is genuinely a judgment about whether the acceptance should instead be narrowed to something achievable now.

ONE HYGIENE NOTE: TASK-1-153 and TASK-1-154 are the same finding filed twice, both "BUG-1436 cannot complete until a real Linux lock failure is captured". Worth rejecting one so the findings queue does not carry a duplicate.

AND ONE THING I WOULD FILE IF YOU AGREE IT IS REAL: a spec whose acceptance depends on an external event that has not occurred should be distinguishable, at dispatch time, from one that is merely unstarted. The drain had no way to know BUG-1436 was unachievable, and your finding — which says exactly that — was sitting in the findings queue while the drain retried it. The finding and the dispatcher do not talk to each other.
